newsitem.title: FINLAND: Metra says has no plans to sell Sanitec.
newsitem.headline: Metra says has no plans to sell Sanitec.

text.p: Finnish engineering group Metra Oy Ab said on Thursday it has no plans to divest its bathroom ceramics unit, even though the group will become almost solely a diesel engine maker after its planned deal with Fincantieri.
"We don't have such plans," Metra executive vice president Ole Johansson told Reuters when asked if Metra would divest the Sanitec unit to focus more on diesels.

Metra earlier unveiled a tentative agreement to merge its Wartsila Diesel with Italian Fincantieri's diesel operations, which would raise diesel operations' share of Metra's net sales to about 80 percent from 65 percent in 1995.
"We have stated clearly that Metra's strategy is to strengthen and develop its main divisions Wartsila Diesel and Sanitec," Johansson said.
"Let's see how we can further develop Sanitec. Our starting point is that we will continue to develop it," he said.
Sanitec accounted for 24 percent of Metra's 10.6 billion markka net sales in 1995.
Metra said earlier the new diesel subsidiary would be the largest in its field worldwide with consolidated proforma 1996 net sales of about 11 billion markka, up from 9.4 billion markka in 1995.
Metra's Wartsila Diesel unit's 1995 net sales were 6.9 billion markka.
